Extract Eligibility and route them based on specificity. If values are provided separately for Class 1, Class 2, and/or Class 3 services, populate only the corresponding class-level fields and leave the general Eligibility field blank. Do not duplicate values into the general row.
If only a  Eligibility value is stated without class distinctions, populate only the general Eligibility field and leave all Class 1, Class 2, and Class 3 fields blank.

Extract any explicit employee-group descriptor that applies generally to all eligible employees
and is NOT tied to a specific class number.

This field captures broad eligibility groupings only when classes are not defined.

Examples include:

- All Eligible Employees
- All Non-US Employees

entities.criteria: Text describing which employees are eligible for LTD coverage and how eligible employees are grouped into classes, including employment status, hours worked, waiting period, and class definitions.

Description of employee group classified as Class 1 for eligibility purposes. 

Extract the explicit employee-group label assigned to Class 1.

If the document distinguishes employee groups by pay type (Hourly vs Salaried):

 output: Hourly Employees for Class 1.
If the document labels Hourly as Class 2, reassign it to Class 1 in output.
If pay type is not used, extract the explicit Class 1 label exactly as written.

Rules:
Capture only the group identity.
Normalize pay-type classes so Hourly = Class 1.
Do not include eligibility mechanics.

Other valid Class 1 group labels include:
- Executives and VPs
- Full Time Employees
- All Non-US Employees

Description of employee group classified as Class 2 for eligibility purposes.

Extract the explicit employee-group label assigned to Class 2.

 output: Salaried Employees for Class 2.

If the document labels Salaried as Class 1, reassign it to Class 2 in output.

If pay type is not used, extract the explicit Class 2 label exactly as written.

Rules:
Capture only the group identity.
Normalize pay-type classes so Salaried = Class 2.
Do not include eligibility mechanics.

Other valid Class 2 group labels include:
- Full Time Employees
- Part Time Employees
- All US Employees

Description of employee group classified as Class 3 for eligibility purposes.

Extract the explicit employee-group label assigned to Class 3, if present.

Valid labels include job category, employment type, or geography.

Apply the same rules as Class 1 / Class 2.

Extract the disability definition wherever it appears in the document. If definitions match across documents, the summary must reflect identical results and must not return null.

Identify the Partial Disability benefit type based on how benefits are calculated.

If benefits are based on percentage of earnings lost, classify as
"Proportionate (Residual) Loss"

If benefits increase by stages or over time independent of earnings loss, classify as
"Progressive Partial Disability"

Do not infer “progressive” unless explicitly stated.

Criteria used to determine ongoing disability based on post-disability earnings or work capacity.

Normalize the gainful earnings threshold into the format:
Own Occupation % / Any Occupation %.

If only one percentage is stated and no distinction between own and any occupation is made, apply the same percentage to both (e.g., 80% → 80% / 80%).

If separate percentages are stated for own and any occupation periods, reflect both values accordingly (e.g., 80% own and 60% any → 80% / 60%).

Standardize formatting as percentages with a space-separated slash (e.g., “80% / 80%”).

Extract any explicit limitation on benefit duration that applies to disabilities
described as self-reported or subjective in nature, including language such as
"self-reported symptoms," "subjective symptoms," or conditions defined as
primarily based on the insured’s report of pain, fatigue, or similar symptoms.

Return duration only (e.g., 24 months).

Do not infer self-reported limitations from mental illness, substance abuse,
or condition lists unless the policy explicitly ties the limitation to
self-reported or subjective symptoms.
Limitations on benefit duration for disabilities caused by mental or nervous conditions. Return duration only (e.g., 24 months).
Limitations on benefit duration for disabilities related to substance or alcohol abuse. Return duration only (e.g., 24 months).
Benefit provision encouraging return to work while receiving LTD benefits. Return duration only (e.g., 24 months).

queries.details:
Premium details exactly as it is written on the document. Premium Calculation Rules:
Monthly and Annual Premium fields are calculated outputs and must never be populated directly from carrier documents.
Any premium values found in documents are reference-only and must not be extracted. Monthly and Annual Premiums must always be whole-dollar amounts.

entities.criteria:
Extract the covered payroll or benefit volume used for pricing (the exposure base). This value represents volume, not cost.
Do not extract rates, premiums, or percentages for this field.
Only populate this field when the document explicitly identifies covered payroll, benefit volume, or exposure used for pricing.
Source this value from the Renewal document and apply the same value across all carriers (Current, Renewal, and Alternative).

Total monthly LTD premium. Do not extract from the document.
Calculate as:
Rate × (Estimated Monthly Volume ÷ rate basis unit)
Example: If rate basis is per $100 of payroll, divide volume by 100 before applying the rate.

After calculating the Monthly Premium using the approved formula, round the result to the nearest whole dollar.
Do not retain cents.

Total annual LTD premium. Do not extract from the document.
Calculate as:
Monthly Premium × 12.

Do not copy carrier-stated annual premiums. Do not independently round the Annual Premium and do not derive it directly from volume.

Percentage increase or decrease from prior LTD rates. 
If a percentage change is explicitly stated, return that value.

Otherwise calculate as:
(Renewal Rate − Current Rate) ÷ Current Rate × 100
The Client Name as stated in the LTD plan,

Extract the plan effective date or coverage period exactly as stated in the document. Look for effective dates on the front cover, first page, Summary of Benefits (SOB), benefit plan year section, or within “amended and restated as of” language. Capture the date text as written and do not substitute eligibility language.

queries.details: Extract any and all source language that defines employee eligibility and dependent eligibility/definitions. Capture eligibility rules whether written as Q&A, headings, bullets, tables, or narrative. Include: (1) employee definition/eligible class (full-time/part-time, scheduled hours, hours/week or hours/month), (2) waiting/probation/eligibility waiting period (not the benefit elimination period payable after disability) and when eligibility is met, (3) coverage effective date trigger (e.g., date of hire, 1st of month following eligibility, 91st day, first day after waiting period), (4) active-at-work/active service requirement that delays coverage, and (5) rehire/reinstatement/reemployment rules (no new waiting period, prior service counts, return-within X days/months/1 year), including leave/layoff/termination and any explicitly stated windows. Also capture Spouse and Child/Dependent Child definitions (including age limits, disabled dependent extension, student rules) even if located in a Definitions/Dependents section. Do not summarize; copy language verbatim.  Include waiting or probationary period for eligibility only. Do NOT capture the benefit elimination period that applies after disability.

entities.criteria: Extract the heading/label/lead-in line for the captured eligibility language (examples: “ELIGIBLE EMPLOYEES”, “EMPLOYEE ELIGIBILITY”, “DEPENDENT ELIGIBILITY”, “ELIGIBLE DEPENDENTS”, “Spouse”, “Child”, “REHIRE/REINSTATEMENT/REEMPLOYMENT”, “ACTIVE AT WORK”, “WAITING PERIOD”, “EFFECTIVE DATE”). If no heading exists, output the first sentence of the captured eligibility language.

Extract the full relevant paragraph(s)/bullets/table rows verbatim for the anchor above, including all stated numbers/timing (hours/week or month, days, “first day of month”, “date of hire”, “provided actively at work”, “within X days/months/1 year”, “no new waiting period”, “prior service counts”). Include surrounding sentences needed to keep the rule complete. Do NOT capture the benefit Elimination Period that applies after disability begins. Capture only timing language tied directly to eligibility for coverage.

queries.details: Extract the termination provision that states when LTD coverage/insurance ends. Capture termination rules whether written as questions/answers, headings, or narrative clauses (e.g., “Termination of Insurance/Coverage,” “When Insurance Ends,” “Coverage will end,” “Insurance ends,” “Termination Date”). Prioritize rules tied to employment termination / cessation of employment / last day worked / termination date / end of active employment (including end-of-month/pay-period wording if stated). If the document uses “no longer eligible,” also capture any definition of eligibility that explicitly links ineligibility to employment ending. If an employment-termination rule exists, include it even if other termination triggers appear.

entities.criteria: Extract the exact question, heading, or clause label that introduces the termination rule (e.g., “When does coverage end?”, “When Insurance Ends”, “Termination of Insurance/Coverage”, “Coverage will end”). If no label exists, extract the leading phrase that signals the rule (e.g., “Insurance ends…”).

Extract the termination rule text that states the timing + trigger, preserving timing language exactly (e.g., “date of employment termination,” “last day worked,” “end of month,” “end of pay period”). Prefer the clause tied to employment termination when present; otherwise capture the most direct “coverage ends” rule stated.

queries.details: Extract all questions/answers or clause/heading + corresponding provision text that define partial disability and how partial benefits work under LTD. Capture the definition test (material duty + earnings threshold + timing), and prioritize any partial benefit mechanics that indicate an earnings-integrated design (e.g., 20% earnings threshold, benefit+earnings cap such as 100% of BME, reduction-by-excess formula, “incentive to work,” step changes like “after 2 years,” and maximum payable percent such as 85% of BME). Include only information explicitly stated.

entities.criteria: Questions, headings, or clause labels related to partial disability/residual benefits/earnings test/return-to-work and partial benefit calculation (e.g., “Partial Disability,” “Monthly Benefit for Partial Disability,” “Earnings Test,” “Work Incentive”).

The corresponding answer/provision text preserving explicit thresholds and formulas (percent of BME, caps like 100% of BME, reduction rules, timing triggers such as after elimination period or after 2 years).

queries.details: Extract questions/answers (or headings/clauses + provision text) that define Disability/Disabled under the LTD policy. Prioritize capturing the duty-based test (e.g., inability to perform material duties) and any earnings-based test (e.g., earnings must not exceed a stated % of pre-disability/basic monthly earnings). Capture any time-based transitions (e.g., after 24 months any occupation) only if explicitly part of the definition.

entities.criteria: Questions/headings/clauses about the definition of Disability/Disabled, especially those stating material duty requirements and any earnings threshold.
The corresponding definition text, preserving the duty test and earnings threshold wording/percent exactly.

queries.details: Extract the document’s Exclusions & Limitations language for LTD and capture evidence for five high-priority exclusions/limitations. First, identify whether a dedicated exclusions/limitations section exists and extract the heading and the verbatim text that belongs to that section (bullets/paragraphs/table rows) until the next major section break. Then, specifically locate and extract the exact wording (verbatim) for each targeted item if present: Pre-Existing Condition exclusion (include timeframes like 3/12, 3/6/12, etc.), Mental Health & Substance Use Disorder limitation/exclusion (include months if limited), Self-reported symptoms limitation/exclusion (include months if limited), Self-inflicted injury exclusion (present/not), and On-the-job injury/work-related injury exclusion (present/not). Do not infer; extract only explicit text.

entities.criteria: Extract the exact question text if the document is in Q&A form; otherwise extract the closest relevant section heading or subheading verbatim (e.g., “Exclusions,” “Limitations,” “Exclusions and Limitations,” “What’s Not Covered,” “General Exclusions,” “Limitations”). If extracting targeted items, use the closest heading/subheading that introduces that item (e.g., “Pre-Existing Condition Limitation,” “Mental Disorders Limitation,” “Self-Reported Symptoms,” “Self-Inflicted Injury,” “Work-Related Injury”).

Extract the verbatim text under the identified heading/question that contains the exclusions/limitations language. Include the full relevant clause(s) for the overall exclusions/limitations section and for each targeted item when found. Preserve timeframes (lookback/exclusion durations), month limits, definitions, and qualifiers exactly as written. If the section is long, capture the complete list content up to the next major section break; if that is not possible, capture the most complete continuous excerpt that contains the full exclusion list. Do not summarize; do not infer.

queries.details: Extract the document language that defines Maximum Benefit Duration (MBD) for LTD, including tables or narrative clauses. Capture age-based schedules (age bands or specific ages) and the corresponding duration/rule (e.g., “to age 65,” “to SSNRA,” “24 months,” “5 years,” “lifetime”), including any qualifiers such as “whichever is longer/longest,” “but not beyond…,” or similar. If the document is not in Q&A form, treat headings/subheadings or lead-in phrases as the “question” and extract the associated table rows or clause text as the “answer.” Do not infer; extract verbatim.

entities.criteria: Extract the exact question text if Q&A format exists; otherwise extract the closest relevant heading/subheading or lead-in phrase verbatim (e.g., “Maximum Benefit Duration,” “Maximum Payment Period,” “Duration of Benefits,” “When Benefits End,” “Benefit Duration Schedule,” “Age Reductions”).

Extract the verbatim MBD content tied to the question/heading, including full table rows and/or clauses showing age/age range and the corresponding duration/rule. Preserve numbers, age ranges, units (months/years), “to age/SSNRA” wording, and “whichever is longer/longest” language exactly.

queries.details: Extract verbatim document language that defines or applies a gainful occupation/gainful earnings/any occupation earnings threshold test, typically within any-occupation or gainful occupation language. Capture the heading/label/lead-in line where the rule appears (or the first sentence if no heading) and capture the full rule language around it (paragraph/bullets/table rows) including any % thresholds, earnings basis wording (indexed pre-disability/monthly earnings, basic monthly earnings, etc.), and any working vs not working split thresholds if stated. Do not summarize or infer; copy source language verbatim.

entities.criteria: Extract the heading/label/lead-in line introducing the gainful occupation/earnings threshold test; if none, output the first sentence of the rule text.

Extract the full verbatim rule language for the gainful earnings/any occupation earnings test (paragraph/bullets/table rows), keeping all numbers, %s, and earnings-basis wording intact; include surrounding sentences needed to understand the test.

queries.details: Extract verbatim document language that describes return-to-work/work incentive/rehabilitation incentive benefits or incentive periods tied to working while disabled, often in Partial/Residual Disability, Rehabilitation/Vocational, or benefit calculation sections. Capture the heading/label/lead-in line where the rule appears (or the first sentence if no heading) and capture the full relevant rule language around it (paragraph/bullets/table rows), prioritizing any explicit duration wording (e.g., first X months, up to X months). Do not summarize or infer; copy source language verbatim.
